summary: Imagine being a child who has just landed on Mars.  Everything looks exciting, until the sky slowly turns orange. A huge dust storm is coming. The solar panels are losing sunlight, the habitat needs energy, and the astronauts are running out of time.  What would you do? What would you save first?  These are not just questions from a game. They are examples of the real challenges humans may face when living on Mars.  Mars is a beautiful but dangerous planet. Its atmosphere is too thin for humans to breathe, radiation is a serious risk, and dust storms can reduce sunlight. Astronauts must carefully manage oxygen, water, food, and energy. One small decision can affect the safety of the whole crew.  But here is the problem: many children learn about space by reading books, watching videos, or looking at pictures. They discover interesting facts, but they rarely get the chance to use what they learn.  We believe children should do more than just learn about Mars. They should experience its challenges, make their own decisions, and understand why those decisions matter.  That is the problem Mars Vision aims to solve.
details: Mars Vision gives children the chance to explore this question through a 2D educational adventure.Designed for children aged 7–12, the game puts players in the role of young astronauts. They explore Mars, complete tasks, solve problems, and discover what humans need to live on another planet. Scientific information is connected to clear mission goals, helping children understand how to use what they learn.The experience focuses on the challenges of running a small Mars base. Players learn about life support, radiation protection, power, and food production. They explore how essential resources can be produced and managed, and why careful planning matters when supplies are limited. Decisions involve balancing different needs, such as using energy to grow food while keeping essential equipment running.Through these activities, children experience simplified versions of the challenges astronauts could face. Their choices have visible results, giving them opportunities to understand mistakes and try different solutions. Simple controls, clear visuals, and short explanations help make the experience suitable for young learners.
